literal: Those who lack knowledge, themselves upon themselves inflicting harm, even for enemies doing is difficult.
translation: The harm that those who lack wisdom inflict upon themselves is difficult even for their enemies to do to them.
modern: அறிவில்லாதவர்கள் தமக்குத் தாமே செய்து கொள்ளும் துன்பத்தை, அவர்களுடைய பகைவர்களாலும் அவர்களுக்குச் செய்வது கடினம்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the self-destructive nature of foolishness. People who lack wisdom constantly make poor decisions that bring suffering upon themselves. The poet emphasizes that the severity of this self-inflicted harm is so great that even their bitterest enemies would find it difficult to cause them such ruin. Ultimately, a foolish person's own ignorance acts as a far more destructive force than any external adversary.
